rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF RICHARD FREEDMAN
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Accounting #1, Report, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 09/30/2026. Issues necessitating continuance: 1) The ending balance of cash assets in accounts must be verified. Verification is made by original bank or brokerage statements or original bank letters signed by a bank officer with the authority to sign showing the vesting of the account, the date, and the amount of the balance. The statements or letters must encompass, not precede, the ending date of the accounting period (LRSF 14.34.D). 2) Please provide authority to support the request that the trustee of the testamentary trust be responsible for payments of statutory fees and burial costs. 3) Please provide more information regarding the funeral costs for decedent. Any liabilities of the estate must be listed in the accounting.4) If the surviving spouse elects to probate assets that are distributable directly to him/her, pursuant to Probate Code Section 13502, the written statement must clearly state that he/she has been fully informed about the reasons for a probate (rather than, e.g., a Spousal Property Petition) and the consequences thereof, including potential delay and increased fees (LRSF 14.35.I.5). 4) Any party lodging a proposed order in a contested matter must file proof of service of the proposed order on all parties entitled to notice of the petition (LRSF 14.7.A.4). Please address the above issues and delivery courtesy copies of all further filings to this examiner no later than 09/16/2026 to avoid additional continuance.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF BESSIE L. FRANKLIN
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Accounting #1, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 9/16/26. Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) The first accounting for an estate may not exceed two years; it cannot be combined in an amended petition that merely separates accounting periods. Subsequent accounting periods may not exceed three years. The second accounting must be filed after the first accounting is adjudicated. (2) "Amended pleading" means a pleading that completely restates and supersedes the pleading it amends for all purposes; it should not have a preamble that explains why it is being filed (e.g., "due to an examiner's notes"). (3) The $25,000 holdback payment was not a receipt includable in the fee base; it was essentially a disbursement during administration. (4) A cursory review of the first accounting shows that there are still entries not fully described. What automobile? Cash withdrawals totaling $3,040.00. "Consumables" or groceries or meals without any description. Credit card payments totaling $1,638.01. (5) Attorney costs must be itemized, showing the DATE, payee, description, and amount of each cost. (6) The notice of hearing must indicate in item 1 the representative capacity of the petitioner. Please provide courtesy copies of any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 9/2/26. It appears that a second amended petition must be filed that includes ONLY the first accounting period and fully discloses all accounting entries, etc. The examiner is aware that objections have been filed. No courtesy copy has been received yet. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. (NB: In order for this Court to track closed matters, orders to terminate and distribute an estate must begin with the following language: "Order for Final Distribution." [LRSF 14.35 I.6.b.] Except for exhibits, each paper filed with the court must bear a footer in the bottom margin of each page, placed below the page number and divided from the rest of the document page by a printed line. [CRC 2.110(a).] In addition to the requirements of CRC 2.111 and 7.102, all pleadings must show the name and representative capacity, if any, of the party for whom the attorney is appearing, e.g., John Jones, Executor. "Petitioner" or "Respondent" alone is not sufficient. [LRSF 14.15 A.])

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF SAMMIE JUNE NATHAN
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Report, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 9/1/26. Examiner needs more time to prepare hearing notes. (No earlier availability.) There were two, not "multiple", reports of status filed in this case and there were no hearings requiring appearance. The administrator is the sole surviving heir and representative of the other heir's estate; notice of proposed action was not required. Notice of proposed action has nothing to do with ensuring that real property meets all legal and title company requirements; it's to give notice to heirs/beneficiaries of a personal representative's intent to sell the property. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. (The "supplement" filed on 7/23/26 actually amended the petition; however, since the costs were reduced, no further notice will be required. Defective notice is cured simply by giving the proper notice. There is no need to declare in a supplement that correct notice will given.)
